clinical.citation: Developmental and epilepsy spectrum of KCNB1 encephalopathy with long-term outcome (PMID: 32954514)

variants.description: Multiple KCNB1 pathogenic variants (missense and truncating)
phenotypes: Poor long-term psychiatric and behavioral outcome

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic variants identified through international collaboration; missense variants associated with more frequent and severe epilepsy compared to truncating variants
clinical.center_country: International collaboration with support from KCNB1 France family association

clinical.citation: Adaptive behavior and psychiatric comorbidities in KCNB1 encephalopathy (PMID: 34915430)

phenotypes: Stagnation and slowing of adaptive functioning with age

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Confirmed KCNB1 encephalopathy diagnosis; severity of epilepsy phenotype predicted severity of behavioral profile (sensitivity 70%, specificity 90.9%)

clinical.citation: A novel autism-associated KCNB1 mutation dramatically slows Kv2.1 potassium channel activation, deactivation and inactivation (PMID: 39135902)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous variant identified by whole exome sequencing; functional investigation revealed slowing of channel activation, deactivation, and inactivation; familial segregation confirmed (father is obligate carrier with autistic features)

clinical.citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)

phenotypes: Refractory seizures (resistant to standard antiepileptic drugs)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo pathogenic variant identified in infant; demonstrated dominant negative effect on KV2.1 clustering at endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions

phenotypes: Daily or weekly GI symptoms (73% of those with GI symptoms)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Confirmed KCNB1-DEE diagnosis; part of channelopathy-associated DEE cohort

clinical.citation: Altered neurological and neurobehavioral phenotypes in a mouse model of the recurrent KCNB1-p.R306C voltage-sensor variant (PMID: 38485094)

phenotypes: Epilepsy with variable age of onset and severity

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Most frequently identified recurrent KCNB1 variant; located in S4 voltage-sensing transmembrane domain; affects voltage-sensing without affecting channel expression

clinical.citation: Characterization of a KCNB1 variant associated with autism, intellectual disability, and epilepsy (PMID: 29264390)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Identified by clinical whole-exome sequencing; functional characterization revealed biophysical channel defects in homotetrameric and heterotetrameric channels; partial loss of function relative to wild-type

clinical.citation: Spectrum of K(V) 2.1 Dysfunction in KCNB1-Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorders (PMID: 31600826)

phenotypes: Shifts in voltage dependence of activation and/or inactivation

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic variants associated with DEE or other NDDs; diverse functional defects demonstrated through high-throughput functional assays

clinical.citation: Clinician's guide to genes associated with Rett-like phenotypes-Investigation of a Danish cohort and review of the literature (PMID: 29023665)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic variant identified in Danish cohort of 35 patients with Rett-like phenotypes; first report linking KCNB1 to Rett-like phenotype

clinical.citation: ASHG 2015 - Whole exome sequencing of family trios identifies novel genes in children with Rett syndrome (RTT) phenotype
clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo heterozygous mutation identified by whole exome sequencing in MECP2-negative patient with Rett-like phenotype; previously linked to epileptic encephalopathy

model_organism.citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation (PMID: 40332468)
phenotypes: elevated locomotor activity in response to pentylenetetrazol (PTZ)
higher c-Fos fluorescence intensity in telencephalon
spontaneous and provoked epileptiform-like electrographic activity
normal brain anatomy and neuronal circuit organization

model_organism.citation: Abnormal cytoskeletal remodeling but normal neuronal excitability in a mouse model of the recurrent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-susceptibility KCNB1-p.R312H variant (PMID: 39738805)
phenotypes: neuronal damage in multiple brain areas
normal electrical properties of pyramidal neurons
marked differences in actin cytoskeleton remodeling

model_organism.citation: Altered neurological and neurobehavioral phenotypes in a mouse model of the recurrent KCNB1-p.R306C voltage-sensor variant (PMID: 38485094)
phenotypes: frequent long runs of slow spike wave discharges on EEG
slow spike and wave activity reminiscent of Lennox Gastaut syndrome

model_organism.citation: Altered neurological and neurobehavioral phenotypes in a mouse model of the recurrent KCNB1-p.R306C voltage-sensor variant (PMID: 37034689)
phenotypes: altered susceptibility to flurothyl and kainic acid induced-seizures
frequent long runs of spike wave discharges on EEG

model_organism.citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
phenotypes: seizures induced by novel environments and handling
abnormal interictal EEG activity including isolated spike and slow waves
genotype-dependent differences in KV2.1, KV2.2, and AMIGO-1 protein expression

model_organism.citation: Oxidation of KCNB1 channels in the human brain and in mouse model of Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 30050035)
Integrin-KCNB1 potassium channel complexes regulate neocortical neuronal development and are implicated in epilepsy (PMID: 36207442)
phenotypes: impaired neuronal migration of glutamatergic neurons
migratory defects persisting into adult brains
disrupted neuronal morphology and synaptic connectivity
impaired biochemical signaling of integrin-K+ channel complexes

model_organism.citation: Kcnb1 plays a role in development of the inner ear (PMID: 33316259)
phenotypes: impaired proliferation and differentiation of mechanosensory cells
altered transcription of genes involved in K+ metabolism, cell proliferation, cilia development, and intracellular protein trafficking

model_organism.citation: ASHG 2018 - Using zebrafish as a tool to model patient mutations of KCNB1 and its role in epilepsy (M.Y. Dennis, A. Colón-Rodríguez, K. Burbach, E. Ferino, M. Bader, P. Lein, L. Jao)
phenotypes: increased activity (distance moved) in presence of PTZ in heterozygous and homozygous fish
no significant differences in body or head size compared to wildtype

biological.citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation. (PMID: 40332468)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9-generated kcnb1 knockout zebrafish (kcnb1+/- and kcnb1-/-) display impaired swimming behavior, epilepsy-like features, spontaneous and provoked epileptiform activity, and γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation. kcnb1 is expressed in multiple CNS regions including neurons, oligodendrocytes, and microglial cells. Loss of function leads to increased bdnf mRNA expression and elevated c-Fos intensity in telencephalon upon PTZ exposure.

biological.citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant. (PMID: 33132203)
biological.summary: KCNB1-G379R expressed in HEK293T cells shows dominant-negative effects, failing to induce endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions and reducing their formation when co-expressed with wild-type KV2.1. This variant affects the non-conducting structural function of KV2.1 in organizing ER-PM junctions.

biological.citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant. (PMID: 33132203)
biological.summary: Kcnb1G379R/+ and Kcnb1G379R/G379R mice show genotype-dependent differences in KV2.1, KV2.2, and AMIGO-1 protein expression levels. Mutant mice display profound hyperactivity, repetitive behaviors, impulsivity, reduced anxiety, spontaneous seizures, abnormal interictal EEG activity, and increased susceptibility to proconvulsant-induced seizures.

biological.citation: Abnormal cytoskeletal remodeling but normal neuronal excitability in a mouse model of the recurrent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-susceptibility KCNB1-p.R312H variant. (PMID: 39738805)
biological.summary: Kcnb1R312H(+/+) mouse neocortical pyramidal neurons show normal electrical properties and ion-conducting functions compared to wild-type, but marked differences in actin cytoskeleton remodeling as measured by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and biochemistry. This indicates the pathogenic mechanism involves non-ionic, structural functions of the channel.

biological.citation: Functions and clinical significance of KCNB1 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. (PMID: 39893596)
biological.summary: KCNB1 knockdown in KYSE70 and TE5 esophageal cancer cell lines inhibits cell proliferation, G2-M phase progression, migration, and invasion while inducing apoptosis. Microarray analysis shows KCNB1 regulates ephrin receptor signaling by suppressing EPHB1, EPHB2, and ERK1/2 expression, controlling cell proliferation through ERK1/2 regulation.

biological.citation: Role of KCNB1 in the prognosis of gliomas and autophagy modulation. (PMID: 28144039)
biological.summary: KCNB1 induces autophagy in glioma cells through the ERK pathway, as confirmed by selective ERK1/2 inhibitor (U0126) and siERK1/2 studies. KCNB1 activation leads to increased apoptosis and reduced proliferation and invasion. In vivo studies show KCNB1 induces autophagy while inhibiting tumor growth and increasing survival.
biological.sample_size: glioma cell lines and in vivo models

biological.citation: Gain-of-function enhancer variant near KCNB1 causes familial ST-depression syndrome. (PMID: 40208226)
biological.summary: A non-coding variant 18 kb downstream of KCNB1 creates a MEF2-binding site that enhances transcriptional activity and interacts with the KCNB1 promoter, as confirmed by 4C chromosome conformation capture in AC16 cardiomyocytes and human muscle tissue. dCas9-activator/repressor assays show KCNB1 is the only gene consistently regulated by this locus.
biological.sample_size: 67 FSTD patients (20 families), AC16 cardiomyocytes, human tissue
biological.significance: perfect co-segregation with ECG phenotype, full penetrance

biological.citation: A KCNB1 gain of function variant causes developmental delay and speech apraxia but not seizures. (PMID: 36618935)
biological.summary: KCNB1 p.P17T variant shows gain-of-function properties in whole-cell patch-clamp recordings: increased current, rightward shifts in steady-state inactivation curve, and reduced sensitivity to guanxitoxin-1E blocker. This gain-of-function is associated with developmental delay and speech apraxia but notably without seizures.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Whole exome sequencing in epilepsy reveals significant gene burden of ultra-rare deleterious variants. (Y. Feng, on behalf of the EPI Collaborative)
biological.summary: Gene-based burden tests in the Epi25 Consortium identified KCNB1 as significantly enriched for ultra-rare protein-truncating variants and damaging missense variants in epileptic encephalopathy patients compared to controls (OR=27.6, p=2e-05). KCNB1 was re-captured as an established epilepsy gene alongside SCN1A and STXBP1.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Dissecting heterogeneity of neurodevelopmental disorders using seed centric genetic modules. (J.C. Chow et al.)
biological.summary: Modules seeded with epilepsy gene KCNB1 are significantly associated with long-term potentiation, synaptic vesicle cycle, and calcium signaling pathways. These modules show significant enrichment of de novo non-synonymous mutations and coding copy number variants in autism, intellectual disability, developmental disability, and epilepsy cohorts.
biological.sample_size: large cohorts of probands with neurodevelopmental disorders
biological.significance: significant enrichment of de novo mutations within modules

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic variants in KCNB1 are modestly associated with type 2 diabetes in American Indians from the Gila River Indian Community. (M. Traurig et al.)
biological.summary: An intronic 16 bp deletion in KCNB1 (mAF=0.02) was associated with protection from type 2 diabetes in Pima Indians (OR=0.51, p=1.2×10-3). A common variant rs3827088 (mAF=0.31) showed association with increased T2D risk (OR=1.17, p=4.9×10-3), replicated in independent American Indian cohort (combined OR=1.18, p=2.5×10-4). Conditional analysis suggests independent effects of both variants.
